meaningMnemonic: The radical is the same as the kanji, so it means body . Just in case you need a refresher, here's the mnemonic again: When your self goes down a slide and hits a barb, it's a painful reminder that you have a body. Sometimes people think their self is just some kind of floating, disembodied consciousness, but getting a barb stuck in oneself while going down a slide will quickly remind one of one's bodily existence.
This looks like a bunch of books on a shelf. It's a bookshelf !

It's kind of hard to see, but if you look at this the right way it looks like a food can . See the lid being pulled off in the top-left corner? And that horizontal line in the middle? That’s the can's label.

This is the radical for canine , because it looks like a police dog — aka a K-9 — marching around on patrol. You can see its proud little head on the top right, its front legs below crossing as it walks, and a police vest labeled "K-9" strapped around its body. Evil-doers beware — this canine's gonna sniff you out and bring you to justice. Alternately, you could see the F-shape on the left as a cheerful canine on its hind legs dancing with a drunkard, arm in arm as they sway along together. What a happy canine, dancing like that with a drunk person.

This radical is the same as the kanji. It means circle . Just in case you don't remember this, here's the kanji meaning mnemonic: What's something with nine sides? Just add a drop and you'll have something that's almost a circle .
Someone's lying on the ground with his mouth open hoping to swallow up passers-by. This guy's a weirdo — a real creeper .

There's a rice paddy on top of a tree… Figuratively, because trees don't bear rice, they bear fruit ! Use your imagination, and those four little boxes on top of the tree kind of look like big, ripe fruits — just waiting to be picked.

This radical is the same as the kanji. It means good . Just in case you don't remember this, here's the kanji meaning mnemonic: A drop of water to a root is good . It's good for the roots to grow and live and thrive. And what's good for roots is good for our plants and us humans too.
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means hundred .
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means idea .

See that cliff with the white and small bits in it? That's an original cliff — we call it that because the white and small bits are actually the bones and fossils of our planet's original inhabitants, buried in the cliffside. (And this one's got a massive sign that says "ORIGINAL," because everything's gotta be a tourist spot these days… sigh.)
You see three squares stacked neatly together. On closer inspection, you realize these are boxed products waiting to be shipped out.
This radical has a little head, a curved abdomen, and some long, spindly antennae sticking out from its nose. There's no mistaking it — this little guy is a shrimp !
You spot a wispy shape flanked by ethereal orbs of flame. Don't be scared — this is just a friendly little soul on its way to get reincarnated into a new body.

Legs appear between two lumps of dirt. This is the earth's version of a womb . Imagine a tiny baby growing under the ground and then sprouting out, legs first, into the world. Imagine being inside this dirt womb. It's warm and damp. You feel safe.

If you compare white light to the other colors you'll realize... white consists of all the colors in one. It contains all the colors in the spectrum in one color. It is the one color that is everything . Hints Just look at the color white. Compare it to other colors. Now look at white again. Split it up into all the colors, creating a beautiful spectrum. Wow, it's all the colors!
readingMnemonic: You decide white light is the ultimate color. You decide you want to put it on all things to make everything white. "What a great idea," you think. You try to put it on everything and you nearly succeed... except, the miners ( みな ). They keep getting dirty doing all their mining things. NOOO, your plan is ruined! Hints Imagine everything covered in white. Everything in the world. Then, you see a dark splotch. It's the miners, they're all covered in coal, ruining all your ambitions. Walk up to them and see all the dirt on the perfectly white uniforms you gave them just a few minutes earlier. Feel enraged at them. How could they ruin all this white you made for all the people of the world!?

meaningMnemonic: You thought it would be a good idea to say the body measurement s of everyone in your village and now you have to apologize . Hints When you do a bad thing you should apologize. And saying everyone's private body measurements is definitely something you should not have done. So it's apology time.
readingMnemonic: You were told you had to apologize by the village sha man ( しゃ ). At first you didn't even know why everyone was glaring at you, but the shaman took you aside and explained. And now she's standing behind you with her arms crossed as you apologize to everybody. Hints "What do we say?" the shaman says, poking you in the back. "Ugh, I'm sorry I told everyone how tiny your socks are, I guess." "And?" "Annnddd I'll never do it again."

meaningMnemonic: A bundle in winter is the correct way to arrange things. Just make sure you organize it all before winter comes, or it'll be too late. Hints Picture all the things you've arranged correctly ahead of winter — logs bundled for the fire, blankets for the night, and yourself, all bundled up in your neatly organized home — just as the first snowflakes begin to fall.
readingMnemonic: But the most important things to arrange and organize are your sa bers ( せい ). You have an extensive saber collection that you simply must organize before winter arrives. Hints Last winter you tripped and fell on a saber you'd left lying around. Ouch, lesson learned. That's when your passion for organizing things in bundles started. You know better than anyone the value of arranging your sabers as safely and tidily as possible.

meaningMnemonic: This tree must've been sent from heaven , because it has a mouth and a mustache . Like some kind of special heaven tree that talks. And why was it sent? To be a bridge . To be the great heavenly bridge that we all, someday, must cross. Hints Picture this majestic tree bridge laid on its side, beckoning you into heaven with its mustachioed mouth. "Cross over!" it says in its bridge voice. Do… do you just step over the mouth? Can you wipe your shoes on the mustache, like it's a bristly doormat to heaven?
readingMnemonic: Actually, to get across this bridge you have to give it some hash ( はし ) browns. That's what the bridge's mouth is for. Hash browns to get across the heaven bridge? Small price to pay, really. Hints Hear the bridge shouting "HASH BROWNS" in its bridge voice. You stuff some hash into its mouth and it starts to chew loudly. Oh, ew… Little hash brown bits are getting stuck in its mustache. Fortunately, the bridge lets you across. Unfortunately, it turns out all of heaven smells like hash browns.

meaningMnemonic: The radical can is the same as the kanji can . Usually when we talk about a can with this kanji we mean a tin can , though. Hints Picture a tin can in your mind as clearly as you can.
readingMnemonic: The reading for a can is かん , which seems impossibly easy. If that isn't close enough for you, picture this: Genghis Khan ( かん ) is drinking out of a tin can. He glug glug glugs, gasps, and wipes his face. He holds out the can, "Khan made cans," and winks. Hints かん is can, it's really easy, come on. Just take this one.

meaningMnemonic: You want to get a scooter , so you have one self ( oneself ) and another self working together to choose . The two tiny yous sit on each of your shoulders, like angel and devil, and argue about which scooter you should choose. Hints Your angel self says you should choose the safest scooter. The devil self says safety is for suckers, and you should buy one that's loud and dangerous and covered in flames.
readingMnemonic: Suddenly your selfs both gasp and choose a scooter in front of you that looks like a cen taur ( せん ). The scooter is designed like a human on the top, the bars are its arms, and the bottom with the seat and the wheels are all horse. This centaur scooter is what you choose to ride. Hints The angel self says, "I choose this centaur scooter because of its strong arms." The devil self says, "I choose this scooter because it looks like a badass horse monster, wooh!"

meaningMnemonic: Big products need to be put in a big container . A small container just won’t do. These products are big and they need a big container to be contained in. Hints Imagine having all these big products. How will you contain them all!? Imagine yourself stuffing all of these big products into their respective containers.
readingMnemonic: Once you get the big products into a container , you then lock it with a key ( き ). You wouldn’t want these products to bust out of their containers, so it’s best to lock them up with a key. Hints Imagine the size of these big keys you have to use to lock these containers. It’s a really big key. Picture yourself straining to turn the key in the lock.

meaningMnemonic: If the sun starts to make a sound , you know it's about to go dark . The sun isn't supposed to make a sound, so if you can hear it, it's probably about to fizzle out or something. After it's gone, obviously everything will be pitch black. Get ready to be in the dark! Hints Imagine a weird sound coming from the sun. Maybe a rumble, or something like a balloon deflating? Then everything goes totally dark. Welp, guess you'll be living in the dark for the rest of your life.
readingMnemonic: Now wandering around your house in the dark you start to feel hungry, so you reach blindly for some food and take a bite. Yuck! It's an chovies ( あん ). You don't even like anchovies, how did they get in your house? Hmm… Dark forces are at work here… Hints And because it's so dark, the anchovy taste is all you can concentrate on. Imagine that fishy, salty taste on your tongue, the little softened bones sticking between your teeth. Ugh.

meaningMnemonic: You reach for a spoon to start eating, but your mama hands you an arrow instead and points towards the coat rack . Hm, that's not like her… Suddenly you're filled with doubt . Is this really your mama? You doubt it. Hints She's just acting so weird. You doubt she would ever make you hunt for your own meal like this. What are you going to do?
readingMnemonic: Now full of doubt , you decide to test your mama by putting her in a gui llotine ( ぎ ). It sounds harsh, but the guillotine is the only way to clear up your doubts. Hints With her head in the guillotine, it's your mama who starts to look doubtful now. "How could you ever doubt me?" she cries. Ugh, now you're really not sure. This guillotine thing has just compounded your doubts.

meaningMnemonic: You have a rice ladle that's specifically for paying the rice fee . Each scoop of something has an extra fee tacked on, so when you use a material , there's a fee you have to pay in that material as well. Hints Imagine ladling up a nice big scoop of rice and then seeing the little fee ladle next to it. Ugh. The material fee.
readingMnemonic: One day, the fee ladle is suddenly the size of row ( りょう ) boat oars! What! You're supposed to pay a row boat sized fee now?! Hints That's a lot of material you have to give up every time you want to eat some rice. Maybe you should take this row boat oar ladle and row out into the ocean where no one can tax you.

meaningMnemonic: Your soul is blue . As in, it's sad and not feeling well. This is because your soul changes colors depending on your feeling s or what emotion s you're expressing. Hints Start with a blue soul. What feeling is that? Now a red soul. What emotion is that? Go through as many colors as you can think of, focusing on the fact that each color represents a different emotion or feeling.
readingMnemonic: Why is your soul feeling blue? Because Joe ( じょう ), the big local farmhand, was extremely mean to you. Hints Maybe he was just having a bad day, but that still really hurt… and now your soul’s all blue too. Seems you’ll have to walk around with a blue soul for the next few days.

meaningMnemonic: When a canine puts its mouth on your heart , it's a pretty unforgettable feeling . Hints The feeling is kind of hard to describe. On the one hand it's warm and loving, but on the other hand it's also kind of wet and slobbery.
readingMnemonic: Overall, though, it's a good feeling — so good that you feel like Genghis Khan ( かん )! With this canine lovingly slobbering on your heart, you feel like you could go out and conquer the world! Hints Just be careful not to let in all the Genghis Khan feelings. The confidence and motivation are good, but the feeling of wanting to wantonly slaughter your enemies is probably one you ought to repress.

meaningMnemonic: By a tree , there's a sheep in the water with a formal name ender . That means everyone calls him Sheep-sama. No one calls him just "Sheep," since he's kind of a big deal. He's actually like sheep royalty. When he's not in his castle, Sheep-sama enjoys playing in the water by the trees. This can also mean manner , as in your manner of doing things. I guess someone with a formal name ender has a different manner of doing things. Hints Imagine what Sheep-sama must have done to become such important and distinguished sheep royalty. Some pretty amazing things, probably, especially for a sheep.
readingMnemonic: This sheep with the formal name ender only likes to play outside in the water during the summer ( さま ). Summer is the best season for this fancy sheep. The other seasons just can't compare. Hints Imagine playing in the water with Sheep-sama in the summer. It's crazy hot outside in the summer, so going in the water feels nice. Imagine the coolness of the refreshing water envelop your body.

meaningMnemonic: Sheep fins are good for foster children. The sheep have been genetically combined with fish, so the sheep have fins (and they've lost their tails — which is why the tail part of the sheep radical is missing in this kanji). These sheep fins are rich in nutrients, so they're good for fostering big, strong foster children. Hints Imagine eating a fish fin with sheep wool on it. It tastes fishy like the ocean but the wool tastes like clothes. It's probably the worst thing ever, but try to imagine you're tasting it right now.
readingMnemonic: The best way to foster a better relationship with these foster kids would be to give them some yo gurt ( よう ). Maybe they can dip the sheep fins in the yogurt to help mask the strange taste. Yogurt is also very nutritious, so it's a good supplement to the foster kids' diet. Hints Remember how bad those sheep fins tasted? Now imagine eating your favorite yogurt flavor instead. This yogurt is delicious.

meaningMnemonic: If you tie a thread around Wolverine and dip him in water , he'll turn green , like the Hulk. Some kind of weird chemical reaction. But I… I wouldn't try it if I were you. You wouldn't like him when he's green. Hints Still, imagine pulling Wolverine from X-Men out of the water with that thread, and seeing him looking kinda green. Pretty green, but he could be greener. We have to go greener! We have to make the Hulk green with envy! So you put him back in the water, again and again…
readingMnemonic: As the flailing Wolverine begins to turn even more green , he calls out, "HELP ME DORY ( みどり )!" Me, Dory? No, not you. He's calling out to that fish from Finding Nemo, another Disney IP. "Help me Dory, I'm green!" Then Dory leaps out of the water to bite through the thread and save Wolverine… THE END. Fade to green. Hints These Marvel crossovers are getting ridiculous.

meaningMnemonic: Your womb spins in a circle and starts to boil with heat . Uh oh, I think you have a fever . Hints Even if you don't have a womb, just picture one anyway: it's turning around in a circle faster and faster, as the heat bubbles and boils in you. You can feel this heat spread through your entire body as you burn up with a fever.
readingMnemonic: The heat from your fever is making your insides and your head and your entire body spin and boil, until your doctor throws some nets ( ねつ ) around you. You were flailing around and they couldn't get you to stop, so they had to catch you in a series of nets. Hints These nets aren't making the fever heat go away, but they have made the spinning stop at least.

meaningMnemonic: A cult leader has a great idea to recruit a hundred million new members. Since he’s the guy with all the ideas, he is the leader of the cult. His idea is to give every new member a free puppy. He’ll have a hundred million new recruits in no time. Hints Imagine a hundred million free puppies. That’s a lot. Imagine playing with all of them. You’d be pretty happy. Unless you hate puppies. Then you’d be pretty unhappy, I imagine.
readingMnemonic: The cult leader has his headquarters in Ok lahoma ( おく ). Are there a hundred million people in Oklahoma? No, probably not. But hey, this leader is shooting for the stars. First Oklahoma, then the universe! Hints Picture this cult leader gathering a hundred million people into Oklahoma. It’d be awfully crowded. Imagine yourself being stifled by the bodies of a hundred million other people.

meaningMnemonic: The leader of a big rice paddy is standing in the middle of said rice paddy with an umbrella . Who is this wacky leader? Why, it is I . It is me . Hints Imagine that this leader is you. Be rough about it, because 俺 is the "rougher" version of "I." You should only use it in casual situations or if you're a badass.
readingMnemonic: Why am I standing in the middle of this rice paddy with an umbrella? I'm digging for ore ( おれ ). Hints More accurately, I'm standing here with an umbrella so I don't get wet. My minions are doing the ore digging, but I am watching to make sure they don't slack off.

meaningMnemonic: Only a tree with eye s and a heart has the ability to imagine and to contemplate . For a tree to imagine and contemplate things, it needs eyes to see and a heart to feel. Hints Can you picture a tree without eyes and a heart imagining something? Contemplating? Probably not. To imagine or contemplate, a tree definitely needs eyes to observe and a heart to experience feelings.
readingMnemonic: If a tree can imagine , it likely has a soul ( そう ). Its soul is what makes it possible for the tree to contemplate things, you see? Hints Use your soul to imagine what this tree is imagining with its soul. Is it contemplating the deep mysteries of the universe? Is it imagining where that squirrel has gone off to?

meaningMnemonic: There's treasure in this tree so you take out your weapon and kill it. Hints You didn't just cut the tree down, you stabbed it and sliced it and killed it to death.
readingMnemonic: But after the kill , Satsu ki ( さつ ) appears and yells at you. She likes trees — remember how she protected one in the 札 mnemonic? — so Satsuki's pretty upset you'd kill one like that. Hints Here's that little girl Satsuki again. Remember how you imagined her last time? Try to have a picture of her in your mind so these さつ kanji are easier to remember.

meaningMnemonic: The roof under which the leader can house one hundred of his people is at the local lodge . Hints Back in the old days a lodge had to be huuuuge so when a leader brought a hundred people through town they'd have a place to stay.
readingMnemonic: The lodge shook ( しゅく ) as the hundred people came tumbling in through the door. It shook, but it didn't fall over. The roof stayed firmly in place, and everyone got to sleep under it okay. Hints Imagine being someone staying at the lodge as they came in and everything shook around you. This lodge would probably last through an earthquake too!

meaningMnemonic: Gold reveals itself when you stand and see into this mirror . Yes, even you are made of gold. You're so great and valuable, standing in front of that mirror. It's not hard to see, especially in a mirror – you're golden. Hints Imagine looking at yourself in the mirror only to see you're made of gold. It would be pretty shocking. Imagine how surprised you would be.
readingMnemonic: As you look into the mirror you think, " Kaga … me ( かがみ )?" You always forget that you're Chairman Kaga from the Iron Chef TV show. That's why you say "Kaga… me?" every time you look in the mirror. Hints Picture yourself in front of a mirror, except your reflection is Chairman Kaga Takeshi. (Look up his picture if it helps.) Imagine not recognizing yourself at first, how weird that would feel, then suddenly remembering: "Kaga… me!"

meaningMnemonic: Under a misshapen crescent moon , a dog boil s as much nature as it can find. Hints Picture a weird-looking, misshapen crescent moon casting its light onto the scene of a dog boiling up everything you'd find in nature. Trees, sticks, mud, little animals. All of that is being boiled by this dog by the light of a weird-looking moon.
readingMnemonic: Destroying nature like this is the dog's way of practicing Zen ( ぜん ) Buddhism. As it breathes in the fumes from all of the different pieces of nature being boiled down, the dog gets really zen and chill. Hints Picture the dog kneeling in front of the pot of concentrated nature and breathing deeply as it practiced Zen. You kind of wish you could join it, considering how peaceful it looks.

meaningMnemonic: What you say at a temple is a poem . It has to be a poem, because if you say anything else it's just plain disrespectful. All of the monks and priests at this temple have to read and recite poems all day, and if they can do it forever, you can while you're visiting. Hints Picture all of the people at the temple reciting poems together. You join in too, and it's a really powerful moment!
readingMnemonic: As you recite a long poem at the temple you see a shee p ( し ) in the crowd. It's opening and closing its mouth like it wants to say the poem too. Hints You turn to the person next to you and realize you have to say everything in poem form. Excuse me I'm not a creep so hear my plea is that a sheep?

meaningMnemonic: Pointing a thread to the east is what you practice every day. You're incredibly passionate about eastward thread-pointing, so you make sure to practice every day. Hints You're absolutely obsessed with pointing your thread towards the east, so all you do is practice. Practice, practice, practice.
readingMnemonic: You do all of this practice to try and afford all of your ren tals ( れん ). One day, all of this practice will pay for all of your rentals. Hints Everything in your life is a rental, so you better get to practicing. Your house, your car, your friends — all of these rentals need to be paid off!

meaningMnemonic: The Viking opens his mouth , and below it, a shellfish sits. Grab that shellfish and throw it into his mouth to win a prize ! Hints Imagine a game at a fair where you have to throw a shellfish into the mouth of a hungry Viking. You want this prize just as much as the Viking wants his shellfish.
readingMnemonic: The prize you're working so hard to win is lunch with the Shou gun ( しょう ). This is a pretty huge prize, considering all you're doing is knocking something over. Hints You want this prize. You want to meet the Shougun. Soon you'll both be eating shellfish together!

meaningMnemonic: If you run into a gate mouth first, you’re going to have a problem . Smashing your mouth into a gate is going to hurt. A lot. The problem you’re now in is one of getting to a hospital and having your mouth sewn back on. The question is, how are you going to get to the hospital? Hints Imagine having your mouth bashed into a gate. It’s going to hurt. Imagine how painful this would be and how problematic it is. Imagine that the only question in your mind is how to get to the hospital as quickly as you possibly can.
readingMnemonic: The reason you ran mouth first into this gate was because you were being chased by a mon ster ( もん ). A monster in and of itself is a big enough problem as is, let alone smashing your mouth into a gate. You poor, hapless soul. Hints Monsters are scary. Maybe you’ve had a dream where you were being chased by one. Remember how scary that is when you see this kanji.

meaningMnemonic: Eat ing the roof is a bear , because the roof is a public building . Because it is a public building bears are allowed to eat the roof. Hints Picture a public building, like a museum or a library, and look at the roof. There's a bear eating the roof!
readingMnemonic: Public building s must make their roofs available for eating because of a law passed by Genghis Khan ( かん ). Hints Imagine Genghis Khan signing something and giving a speech talking about how important it is that all bears are able to eat the roofs of public buildings, as a bear in the background eats the roof.

meaningMnemonic: The samurai radical and the samurai kanji are the same! Hints Know your radicals, yo!
readingMnemonic: The most famous samurai in Japanese history was the illustrious shee p ( し ) samurai. He wasn't JUST a sheep who learned the ways of the sword, he would use the wool from the sheep enemies he killed to create his armor! Hints Picture the sheep samurai. Maybe draw him on a piece of paper. He's a sheep wearing wool armor, and he has ram horns on the hilt of his katana.

meaningMnemonic: I always say the fruit section at the grocery should be at the front of the store. It’s the perfect place for the fruit section, I say. Hints Think about it. Every grocery store has the fruit section right at the front, wouldn’t you say?
readingMnemonic: To get to the fruit section , you have to go to the store. To get to the store you have to drive a ca r ( か ). Driving a car is the fastest way to get to the fruit section at the store. Hints Picture yourself driving a car and salivating over the fruit waiting for you in the fruit section. Imagine your favorite fruit as you put the pedal to the metal in your awesome car.

meaningMnemonic: You see a tree with a helicopter and a jackhammer tied to it. You look closer, because this is an odd sight, and realize that there is a sign here too. It's telling you to beware of helicopters and jackhammers in these woods. It's a poorly made signpost ! Hints This is not the best signpost you've ever seen, but it's better than nothing at all, you suppose.
readingMnemonic: As you look at this weird signpost you notice a button. You press it because it will supposedly tell you more about these dangerous helicopters and jackhammers. Instead, it just yells out in a loud obnoxious voice: HEYO ( ひょう )!! Hints Press it a few more times and hear the sound in your head. Also spell it out in kana as you hear it as a nice little additional visual.

meaningMnemonic: Gold , at its root , is made up of silver . Using silver as the root of a coin is a great way to save on gold! That's why, often, if you just scratch gold, you'll find there's silver hidden underneath, at its root. Hints Imagine taking a gold coin and scrubbing it with some soap and water. As you scrub, you slowly see that it's really silver underneath. Dang it, silver again!
readingMnemonic: If you want to hunt for some silver for yourself, all you need is a guin ea ( ぎん ) pig. Guinea pigs can smell silver, so get a couple and set them loose in the woods and they'll lead you straight to it. Hints Guinea pigs are to silver as normal pigs are to truffles.

meaningMnemonic: A horse and a shrimp are sitting next to each other. They are both at the train station , waiting for a train to come and take them home. Hints Imagine the horse and the shrimp sitting next to each other on a small bench. There is nobody else at the train station. It is awkward.
readingMnemonic: The train pulls into the station . They walk up to the train doors, but they don't open. "Perhaps a key ( えき ) would help?" asks the station master, as he goes over to open the door to the train. Hints Instead of saying "a key" he says "eh key." How strange. Imagine the station master saying it like this with his weird accent. You ask him if he has "a key" and he replies with, "What is a key?" Then you say "eh key." He totally understands you now.

meaningMnemonic: The sun shines down on your coat rack to reveal your geoduck -patterned jacket, which then becomes the major topic of discussion all around town. Hints Everywhere you go, you overhear someone talking about your stylish geoduck-patterned jacket. It's the only topic anyone wants to talk about.
readingMnemonic: After a few days, the topic changes from the cool geoduck design to what kind of dye ( だい ) you used to get those real-to-life geoduck colors. Hints Imagine how annoying it is to constantly be asked about the dye you used in your jacket. You'd really like to change the topic — some might even say you're dye -ing to change it…

meaningMnemonic: For your car you use a hat , some ground and a bookshelf to build a new wheel . I mean, it's generally ring and loop shaped, it just needs to be a circle , so it should work, right? Hints Imagine this wheel you made out of a hat, some ground (presumably to keep it all together), and a bookshelf. You install it on your car and hope for the best. This is why you should buy wheels from professional wheel makers.
readingMnemonic: Your wheel is... generally rin g ( りん ) shaped, so that's good. Hints A ring-shaped wheel is better than nothing. Hopefully it will get you where you need to go.

meaningMnemonic: The fee for enter ing a public building is the admission fee . Gotta pay it if you want to get inside.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.english: need to pay an admission fee
to hand over the admission fee

sentences.english: How much is the admission fee?

sentences.english: The entrance fee here is too expensive.

sentences.japanese: 今日は入館料はいりません。
sentences.english: No admission fee is required today.

meaningMnemonic: If you foster a child for long enough, eventually you'll want to adopt them and make them your adopted child .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.english: to do together with one's adoptee
to make someone one's adopted child
to be adopted into another family

sentences.japanese: 駅長の子は、どうやら養子らしいです。
sentences.english: I heard that the station master's kid is actually an adopted child.

sentences.japanese: 私の友人は、赤ちゃんを養子に出すことにしました。
sentences.english: My friend decided to give her baby up for adoption.

sentences.japanese: 二人は養子をもらって育てました。
sentences.english: The couple adopted and raised a child.

meaningMnemonic: マンション comes from the English word "mansion," but it just means an ordinary apartment building in Japanese. Depending on context, it can also mean an individual apartment . Either way, it’s definitely not a big, luxurious house in Japanese!

sentences.japanese: ウイークリーマンション
sentences.english: an apartment rented by the week

sentences.japanese: ワンルームマンション
マンションのベランダ

sentences.english: the second floor of an apartment building

Because when you arrive somewhere, it's like you're finally attached to your destination. meaningMnemonic: You have the kanji for empty , so this verb means to become empty . Think empty bottles, vacant bathroom stalls, even an open block in your schedule — that sort of thing.

Ah… Your bag of chips is becoming empty? Ah… Exclaiming a little "Ah…" is the only thing that helps you cope with the sadness of your favorite things becoming empty. meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji 受 means accept and this verb is related. It means to get accepted , usually into something good like a university or a new job. It can also mean to pass , often in the context of a test or an exam. This is an intransitive verb, so no direct object is needed. A hint for this is that it ends with okurigana that rhyme with ある , and those kinds of verbs tend to be intransitive. Also, be careful: in English you'd use the transitive expression "pass a test," but in Japanese you'd say 試験に受かる . Kind of like saying you pass in the exam — so it's still intransitive!
readingMnemonic: Since this word has okurigana (hiragana attached to the kanji) you know that it's probably going to be the kun'yomi reading. Here's a little mnemonic to help ya remember: To get accepted into this program, you have to juggle u nis ( う )—yes, those spiky sea urchins! Handling uni is tough, but if you want to pass the test and get accepted, you've got to master the uni challenge.

meaningMnemonic: Remember how 放す is "to release"? Now you're learning the intransitive version. Instead of you doing the releasing, something gets released or freed. So this is to get loose , to escape , or to be released . 放れる describes something held in place coming loose and starting to move, like an animal breaking free from its tether or an arrow being released from a bowstring. You know this because it's pretty rare ( れる ) for something that's restrained to break free from its bonds. Escaping isn't easy, so it only happens on rare occasions.
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same one you learned with 放す . If you can remember that word, you can apply the reading over here as well.

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means kill so the verb vocab version is to kill .
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You kill someone! Oh no, what are you going to do? Where will you put the body? You decide to stuff it into the core ( ころ ) of a nuclear silo. It will melt and disappear in there, right? At least, that's what you think. Imagine opening up the core of the nuclear silo and feel the burn of the radiation. You throw the body in and close the core, then run away. Unfortunately, this nuclear core will kill you too, eventually. Then, it will kill everyone in the area, because the body you threw in will overheat the core, causing a giant explosion.

sentences.japanese: あのハエ、どうやって殺すつもりなの？
sentences.english: How are you planning to kill that fly?

sentences.japanese: お前なんか殺してやる！
うちの子は、虫を殺すこともできないくらい気の弱い子なんです。
sentences.english: My child is so timid that they can't even bring themselves to kill insects.

meaningMnemonic: Your see ing is return ing on something. This verb can be both transitive and intransitive. When it’s transitive, it means to look back at , in the sense of looking back at someone who’s behind you, or looking back at your past. When it’s intransitive, it simply means to look back , in the sense of looking over your shoulder.
readingMnemonic: The readings are just 見 and the vocab word 返る , combined together. So long as you know both of those you should be able to combine them into the reading for this word.

sentences.japanese: チラリと見返ると、彼もまだ私のことを見ていました。
sentences.english: When I glanced back, he was still looking at me.

sentences.japanese: 青緑色のチョウチョウがヒラヒラしているのを見ながら、私はふと森君の方を見返りました。
sentences.english: As I watched the fluttering of the turquoise butterfly, I suddenly glanced back at Mori-kun.

sentences.japanese: ガシャーンと大きな音がして、私は思わず後ろを見返った。
sentences.english: There was a huge crash and I involuntarily looked behind me.

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means separate , so you can guess the meaning is to separate or to be divided .
readingMnemonic: Remember the word 分ける ? That word means "to separate" too. The reading is similar, though not the same, but we can at least use it as a jumping off point. We go from わける to わかれる . It's like we've "separated" the け and the る and combined them in the middle. け , making a かれ , which gets you to わか れる .

will break up soon, will part ways soon
to break up with one's boyfriend
to break up with one's girlfriend

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means solve so the verb vocab version is to solve . You know this verb is for when you are doing the solving because you think it's super coo ' ( く ) to solve things.
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: There's something you've been trying to solve for your entire life: your toe ( と ). Why is it shaped like that? Why is it a little crooked? What's it scheming? Maybe one day you'll solve the mystery of your toe…

sentences.japanese: 私たちは今、この暗号を解くためのヒントをさがしています。

meaningMnemonic: The heaven king star is the planet Uranus . Knowledge of Greek mythology will definitely help you here, because the English name is a reference to the Greek god of the skies, and the Japanese name is a direct translation of that!
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word and uses the on'yomi, but over time the reading for 王 changed from おう to のう , to make it easier to pronounce. You'll still see that listed as an alternative reading in some dictionaries, but it's pretty much never used nowadays, so we'll only accept the てんのうせい reading. Here's a mnemonic to help you remember: Who predicted the discovery of Uranus ? No stradamus ( のう ), of course!

sentences.japanese: 天王星は一回りするのに八十四年かかります。

meaningMnemonic: When たち is attached to a word referring to a person, it makes it plural. So, when you attach たち to 俺 ( I ), it means we or us . Just remember that 俺 is quite casual and rough sounding, so it's best to only use it with close friends (or when you're shaking someone down...).
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

meaningMnemonic: Remember how 風 can mean "style" as in 和風 ? Well, this is now Western style style , more simply put as Western style . 洋風 is used to describe things with a Western look or influence, like 洋風の部屋 (Western-style room) or 洋風スープ (Western-style soup).
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: バターを入れて、うどんを洋風にアレンジしました。
sentences.english: I put butter in udon to give it a western-style twist.
